guidance.framing: Stand 2–2.5 m from the camera at a slight 30° angle so hip, knee, and ankle stay visible.
guidance.calibration_instruction: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart and extend both arms horizontally at shoulder level (T-pose) for 3 seconds.
steps: Begin standing tall with knees near full extension (~165°–175°).
Hinge at the hips and bend knees smoothly toward 70°–95° without letting knees collapse inward.
Pause briefly at bottom flexion, then drive evenly through both heels back to standing.
guidance.form_cues: Keep torso upright (avoids Trunk Lean alert) and hips level (avoids Lateral Pelvic Shift).

guidance.framing: Face the camera 1.5–2 m back with your upper torso, left shoulder, elbow, and wrist clearly framed.
guidance.calibration_instruction: Stand tall and hold a horizontal T-pose for 3 seconds to normalize shoulder-to-hip proportions.
steps: Relax shoulders down and start with the elbow extended (~160°–170°) beside your torso.
Flex the elbow smoothly, bringing the wrist upward toward the shoulder (~35°–50°).
Lower the forearm under control back to full extension without swinging.
guidance.form_cues: Keep your collarbone level and avoid hiking the shoulder upward during peak flexion.

guidance.framing: Stand straight facing the camera 1.5–2 m away so both shoulders and extended arms fit inside the frame.
guidance.calibration_instruction: Hold a steady horizontal T-pose for 3 seconds so shoulder baseline span and trunk midline are calibrated.
steps: Start with arms resting comfortably at your sides (~95° shoulder-to-elbow baseline).
Raise your left arm laterally outward with a straight elbow up to shoulder height (~170°–175°).
Hold 1 second at top abduction, then lower smoothly back to your side.
guidance.form_cues: Avoid leaning your torso sideways or shrugging the shoulder toward your ear.

guidance.framing: Position one hand 35–55 cm in front of the camera with good lighting and an uncluttered background.
guidance.calibration_instruction: Hold your palm open and steady facing the camera for 3 seconds to normalize palm scale and finger aperture.
steps: Start with palm neutral and thumb & index finger comfortably open (~70–90% aperture).
Flex the index MCP/PIP joints and touch thumb tip (#4) cleanly to index tip (#8).
Open smoothly back to the starting neutral aperture to complete each pinch cycle.
guidance.form_cues: Keep the wrist aligned vertically with the forearm to avoid Excessive Wrist Deviation alerts.
